newsitem.title: USA: Sizzler Int'l files reorganization plan.
newsitem.headline: Sizzler Int'l files reorganization plan.

text.p: Sizzler International Inc on Monday said it filed a plan of reorganization and hoped to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection by June 1.

"We're on the road now. My expectation is (a return to profitability) in the next fiscal year," said Chief Financial Officer Christopher Thomas in an interview. "We've completed the restructuring of our U.S. operations, and we're really prepared to move forward now."
Thomas said he expected to return to profitability as early as the first quarter of fiscal 1998, which starts May 1.
"Our goal is in fiscal 1998 to see the company return to profitability," he said.

Sizzler filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection last June, closing 130 unprofitable restaurants and taking a charge of $109 million. Thomas said he did not expect any more charges from the reorganization even though the company closed more restaurants than it had initially planned.
The bankruptcy was unusual in that Sizzler had assets of $272 million and liabilities of just $98 million when it filed for Chapter 11 protection.

Sizzler will emerge from Chapter 11 even leaner than originally planned. At the beginning of February, the company operated 71 U.S. restaurants and had 201 franchise operations. In other countries, it operates 42 Sizzlers and has 92 franchises, three joint ventures, as well as 94 Kentucky Fried Chicken restaurants in Queensland, Australia.
In June, Sizzler said it would keep 85 domestic restaurants and 235 franchises.
In its filing on Monday, Sizzler International said it planned full payment of its creditors' claims, estimated at about $70 million, to be secured by international operations.
